competences: The learner describes distinguishing good and bad advice using religious education vocabulary.
The learner identifies appropriate Christian values in decisions and family relationships.
languageCompetence: Reads, spells and uses advice, peace, trust, marriage, respect, patience, tolerance, faithfulness and vows.
objectives: By the end of the lesson, learners should be able to explain distinguishing good and bad advice.
By the end of the lesson, learners should be able to answer at least three cited exercise questions using the correct facts.
priorKnowledge: Learners have already learned the meaning of friendship and how Jesus demonstrated care, forgiveness, kindness and service to other people.
materials: P6 CRE teacher's notes on friendship and marriage
Chalkboard with source-based definitions and qualities
references: P.6 Religious Education Lesson Notes, Term III (2022)
P6 Religious Education Lesson Notes Term III

steps.teacherActivity: Begin by reviewing distinguishing good and bad advice through one familiar idea from the previous lesson. Ask learners how this week's topic builds upon respectful friendships and responsible choices.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners recall previous work on friendship, explain their existing understanding, and respond to the opening questions.

steps.content: Meaning of advice; Qualities of good advice: **Advice** means an opinion or suggestion on what a person should do. People seek advice when they must make important decisions in life. Friends may help one another make careful and responsible decisions. Not all advice is good, even when offered by someone familiar.
steps.teacherActivity: Explain meaning of advice and qualities of good advice, setting out each definition and fact exactly as given in the source notes. Ask short questions to confirm understanding.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners listen, explain the key meanings, and copy the factual chalkboard points into their notebooks.

steps.content: Bad advice; Importance of good advice: Bad advice encourages people to use abusive words against others. Bad advice may promote hatred and jealousy between friends. Bad advice may encourage people to cheat or tell lies. Bad advice may encourage disobedience and unfaithfulness.
steps.teacherActivity: Teach bad advice and importance of good advice with the examples and differences provided by the source. Ask the learners to compare the ideas and identify correct choices.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners identify and compare source-based facts, name examples from the notes, and explain the main Christian values.

steps.content: Sourced written exercise: Why do we all need advice? | Write down two the qualities of good advice? | How does good advice promote peace? | Give one example of advice which is Godly | How can one distinguish between good and bad advice?
steps.teacherActivity: Give all five existing exercise questions to the class without changing their numbers or wording. Discuss answers using the original teacher notes after individual work.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners answer the five sourced questions in writing and compare answers with the notes during correction.

steps.teacherActivity: Review the main definitions and key qualities from the chalkboard notes. Ask a final question to identify misunderstandings and assign the sourced exercise questions for revision.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners restate what was learned, correct one answer if necessary, and note the home revision task.

assessment: Check learning from the cited source using the exact questions: Why do we all need advice? Write down two the qualities of good advice? How does good advice promote peace? Give one example of advice which is Godly How can one distinguish between good and bad advice? Correct individual answers in class, then give revision feedback.
homework: Answer two of the sourced questions again at home, using the teacher's facts and notes.
